identity.note: The GIWF's "Jack of AmWt" (1999) is folded in here as a presumed match. This record's own IWF bio page bills him "Tag Team: AmericaZ MosT WanteD TeaM". His partner's page says Busta Rap Shawn is "Now a member of AmWt". The IWF's tag-team rankings list "AmWt (Busta Rap/Jo Daddy Jack)" as "#1 Contenders North American Tag Titles", and its home page lists "North American Tag Team Titles: AmWt". The GIWF was founded in February 1999 by the handler who played Coma in the IWF. It writes the same abbreviation with the same capitals and gives it the same two men: "Jack and Shawn of AmWt" (6 April 1999) and "America's most wanted Team" (30 March 1999). The UWF's all-time roster keeps "Jack (AmWt w/ Shawn)" and "Shawn (AmWt w/ Jack)". Other IWF characters reappear on the GIWF's 1999 cards in the same way, including John Constantine, Sandman, Akira, Yoshihiro Tenzan and the Grim Reaper. The GIWF gives no vital (height, weight, style) to test against this record's IWF card. Its Jack's named move is the "JACK-knife Power Bomb", which does not contradict the IWF's Da BomB, a double-team finisher. No document names both records, so the grade is presumed and not primary-source. The UWF's all-time roster also has a separate line for "Jack Blarney (Irish Hood w/ Cluney C.)". This record's IWF card reads "Real Name: Jack Blarny", and whether that later Irish Hood Jack is this man is not ruled here.

notes: PROVENANCE — the name was inherited twice over. This collection's Lew Spectre took the name from a character in a lost, earlier fed, which had in turn taken it from a real Florida wrestling figure (see the external entity lew-spectre-original). Three Lew Spectres; no shared identity between any of them. The name is truly his — this collection's, by the time it reached him, free and clear. (The identity of the intermediate handler who carried the name between the real figure and this collection is deliberately not named here.) Kayfabe father of Corky Spectre (UiWF) — a fictional relation the registry records as a story fact, not an identity merge. THE LOST FIRST FED, FOUND: NCCW — New Classic Championship Wrestling (see the frontier's own row), live by the 1998 RSPWF year-end rankings, folded c. 2000/01; its Lew Spectre ranked #156 with the [NCCW] tag in the 2000 RSPWF Top 200, and the fed's own World Title scene carried the Cameron–Spectre feud. The name's whole chain now stands receipted end to end.
